java.say: Someone asks a borrower for the total of its open fines. Borrower knows all its loans, so it is the expert for the total.
It does not work out each fine itself. It asks each loan for its own fine and adds them up.
A loan knows its book and its due date, so it is the expert for its own fine.
It counts the days from the due date to today.
When the book is late, the fine is the days late times the fine per day. Otherwise it is 0.
The fine per day belongs to the book, so the loan asks the book for it. Each class works with the data it has.

cpp.say: Someone asks a borrower for the total of its open fines. Borrower knows all its loans, so it is the expert for the total.
It does not work out each fine itself. It asks each loan for its own fine and adds them up.
A loan knows its book and its due date, so it is the expert for its own fine.
It counts the days from the due date to today. Both are dates counted in days, so subtracting them gives a number of days.
When the book is late, the fine is the days late times the fine per day. Otherwise it is 0.
The fine per day belongs to the book, so the loan asks the book for it. Each class works with the data it has.
